claims.text: Greg Short asserts that an aspiring entrepreneur in 2026 does not need any startup capital to begin monetizing knowledge, because knowledge combined with effort can be packaged and delivered digitally at near-zero cost. The constraint on entry is skill and sweat, not money.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: knowledge or expertise exists in any domain
digital delivery is possible (PDF, digital guide)
founder has a laptop and time
claims.mechanism: Knowledge packaged as a digital product has zero marginal cost of replication; each additional copy sold requires no additional inventory, manufacturing, or capital outlay.
bounded_by: Does not apply to physical product businesses where inventory or manufacturing cost is required
Does not apply to businesses requiring regulatory licensing or physical infrastructure

claims.text: Greg Short and his co-founders grew a college dorm-room instant-download PDF workout guide business (sold via PayPal DM for $9.99 each) to hundreds of thousands of PDF sales and hundreds of thousands of weight loss transformations, which then evolved into the Mari Fitness brand, then the Slay app (launched on the Apple App Store on January 1st as the head of Peloton's app store category), and ultimately the Strength app.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

numbers.axis: business evolution milestones from dorm-room PDF to full app

anchors.value: $9.99 PDF sold via PayPal DM, no website or storefront
hundreds of thousands of PDFs sold, hundreds of thousands of weight loss transformations
Slay app listed as head of Peloton on Apple App Store, January 1 launch date

claims.text: Greg Short argues that for an early-stage entrepreneur, the optimal first product is one that costs nothing to make beyond personal knowledge and effort, specifically an instant-download digital product such as a PDF guide. This avoids inventory, manufacturing, and capital risk while still delivering real value.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: founder is early-stage with no capital
founder possesses domain expertise (fitness, weightlifting, etc.)
claims.mechanism: Digital knowledge products have zero variable cost, enabling profit on the first sale; the founder's existing expertise is the asset, requiring no external capital to create.
bounded_by: Does not apply where customers require physical deliverables
Requires that the founder already possesses sellable knowledge or expertise

examples.text: Greg Short and his co-founders started in a college dorm room with no website, no storefront, and no money to buy physical products. They created instant-download PDF workout guides and sold them via PayPal for $9.99 each, sending the PDF by email after payment. The business grew to hundreds of thousands of weight loss transformations and PDF sales, eventually becoming Mari Fitness, then the Slay app (featured as the head of Peloton on the Apple App Store at its January 1 launch), and finally the Strength app — all from a zero-capital, knowledge-only starting point.

practices.text: Sell something that costs you nothing to make other than your knowledge and hard work — an instant-download PDF is the simplest viable form of this in 2026.
Use DM-based selling (social media DM to payment link) as the minimum viable sales infrastructure when you have no website or storefront.
